prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1177; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured vehicle was backing out of a space when it contacted the claimant's vehicle in the adjacent lane. Both drivers reported no police response due to minor visible damage. Photos of both vehicles and the scene requested from the insured.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Representation letter received and noted in file. All further contact to be directed through the attorney's office. Claimant's representative indicated a cervical and lumbar strain with ongoing neck stiffness and lower back discomfort. Medical records requested under signed authorization.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos and repair estimate for claimant's vehicle. Rear bumper cover, tail light assembly, and trunk lid show damage consistent with the reported impact angle. Independent appraisal scheduled. Insured's statement obtained and confirms the vehicle was in reverse at under walking speed when contact occurred.

Entry 4: Received initial treatment records from the claimant's primary care provider showing diagnosis of neck and back strain, prescribed muscle relaxants, and referral to physical therapy. Treatment notes indicate reduced range of motion in the cervical spine. Records forwarded to the medical review desk for evaluation of causation and reasonableness of treatment.

Entry 5: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding status of medical documentation and the physical therapy schedule. Counsel requested that the file remain open pending completion of treatment. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the injury component. Follow-up diary set to review records once the treating physician issues a progress report.
